2027-05-28.title: Second Friday of the Apostles
2027-05-28.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The wisdom of this world is foolishness with God
I am the bread of life
2027-05-28.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), which began at Pentecost: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, carried the Gospel to the nations. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and from Pentecost the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven.
2027-05-28.verse: Very truly, I tell you, whoever believes has eternal life. I am the bread of life.
theo: Yesterday we celebrated the Body and Blood of Christ; today the Gospel takes a step back in the same discourse at Capernaum and shows us the road that leads to the altar. Jesus quotes the prophets: “It is written in the prophets, ‘And they shall all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to me.” The words come from Isaiah's promise to the restored Jerusalem, “All your children shall be taught by the Lord” (Isaiah 54:13). Before anyone eats the bread of life, they must first listen and learn. That is why every Holy Qurbana has two tables: first the table of the Word, with the readings and the homily, and then the table of the Body and Blood. Jesus adds at once that this learning is not mere information: “Not that anyone has seen the Father except the one who is from God; he has seen the Father.” Only the Son has seen the Father face to face. To be taught by God is to be taught by the Son, who makes the Father known.

Then comes the simple, tremendous claim: “Very truly, I tell you, whoever believes has eternal life. I am the bread of life.” Jesus contrasts himself with the gift Israel remembered with gratitude: “Your ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died. This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that one may eat of it and not die.” The manna was a true gift of God; it kept a whole people alive for forty years in the desert. But it fed bodies that would one day die. The bread that Jesus gives, which is himself, feeds a life that death cannot end. Notice that faith comes before eating in this passage: whoever believes has eternal life. The Eucharist is truly Christ whatever our state, but it bears fruit only in a heart that believes. We come to the altar as people who have listened, learned and believed, and the Lord who is received into a believing heart gives life that lasts.

Paul's words to the Corinthians sound at first like an insult: “If you think that you are wise in this age, you should become fools so that you may become wise. For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God.” The Corinthians were proud of their learning and had divided into parties: some for Paul, some for Apollos, some for Cephas. Paul says that boasting about human leaders is foolish, and then he turns the whole question upside down: “For all things are yours, whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future, all belong to you, and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.” The apostles do not own the Church; they serve it. The believer does not belong to a party, a preacher or a movement, but to Christ. In our own day the temptation is the same. We can make idols of favourite preachers, of retreat centres, of a style of liturgy, of a family or a community, and forget that all these are gifts given to us so that we may belong more fully to Christ. To become a fool for Christ is to let God teach us, as children are taught, and to stop measuring the things of God by the wisdom of the market, the media or the examination hall.
outline: Ask: who is teaching me, and do I let God teach me?
Listening before eating: the two tables of the Qurbana.
The manna that kept bodies alive, and the bread that conquers death.
No party, no preacher, no human boast: all is ours, and we are Christ's.
live: Read the Gospel of Sunday's Qurbana at home before you go, so that you come to the table of the Word ready to listen.
Do not boast about human leaders (1 Corinthians 3:21)
If you have taken sides in a quarrel about preachers, priests or movements in your parish, make peace with someone on the other side.
fathers: The Father teaches us by drawing us to the Son. Do not seek a teacher on earth who could lead you to God apart from Christ; the Master is within, and those who are taught by the Father come to the Son as the hungry come to bread.

Paul does not tell the wise to give up their minds, but to give up the wisdom that is puffed up. Become a fool for Christ, that is, let him teach you, and then you will truly be wise; for the one who will not learn as a child will never learn at all.
magis: The liturgy of the Eucharist unfolds as one act of worship: the liturgy of the Word, with the readings and the homily, and the liturgy of the Eucharist, with the presentation of the gifts, the consecration and Communion.
It is in the harmony of the two Testaments that the paschal catechesis of the Lord is built; the manna in the desert prefigures the Eucharist, the true bread from heaven.
Faith is a gift of God, a supernatural virtue infused by him; Jesus says that this revelation does not come from flesh and blood but from the Father who is in heaven.
saints: 26–31 May: second and third weeks of the Season of the Apostles. Wed 26: in the Latin calendar, St Philip Neri. Thu 27: the Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ (the Latin Church in India keeps Corpus Christi on Sunday 30 May). Sat 29: in the Latin calendar, St Paul VI. Sun 30: Third Sunday of the Apostles. Mon 31: the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, which closes the month of Mary. The Sacred Heart of Jesus falls on Friday 4 June.
2027-05-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you alone have seen the Father, and you make him known to us. Teach us, as the prophets promised, so that we may hear and learn from the Father and come to you. You are the bread of life: give us faith to receive you, and life that death cannot end. Deliver us from the wisdom of this world that is foolishness with God, from boasting and from divisions, and keep us always yours, as you are the Father's. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Every Holy Qurbana sets two tables before us: the table of the Word, where God teaches us, and the table of the Body and Blood, where the bread of life is given. Let us listen at the first so that we may receive at the second with faith.

quick: Jesus: they shall all be taught by God; everyone who has learned from the Father comes to me.
Jesus is the bread of life: the manna fed bodies that died; whoever eats this bread will not die.
Paul: the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God; all things are yours, and you belong to Christ.
2027-05-28.action: Read next Sunday's Gospel at home before the Qurbana, and make peace with someone you have quarrelled with over a preacher or a parish matter.
2027-05-28.question: Do I let God teach me, or do I measure the things of God by the wisdom of the world?

family.explain: When the people of Israel walked through the desert, God fed them every morning with manna, a special bread from heaven. But one day they all died. Jesus says that he is a better bread: the bread of life. When we believe in him and receive him in the Holy Qurbana, he gives us a life that never ends, even after we die.
family.intention: We pray for teachers, catechists and all who teach children about God.
family.ask: Ask: “What did God teach us this week through the Bible or through someone?”

illus: A professor of physics at a university in Kerala used to stay behind after Sunday Qurbana to help with the catechism class for six-year-olds. His colleagues teased him: a scientist teaching nursery prayers. One day a student asked him why he bothered. He said that in his laboratory he had learned how much he did not know, and in the catechism room he had learned to be taught. ‘The children ask the real questions,’ he said. ‘Who made God? Where is Grandmother now? Is Jesus really in the Host? I have to go home and pray before I can answer them. In the lab I am the teacher. On Sunday mornings God teaches me through them.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the bread of life, and you teach us the ways of the Father. Open our ears and our hearts as we gather around your word. Amen.
share: They shall all be taught by God (John 6:45). Through whom has God been teaching me lately?
I am the bread of life (John 6:48). How hungry am I for Jesus in the Holy Qurbana?
The wisdom of this world is foolishness with God (1 Corinthians 3:19). Where have I trusted worldly wisdom more than God's word?
All things are yours, and you belong to Christ (1 Corinthians 3:21, 23). Do I live as one who belongs to Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, bread of life, teach us and feed us.
interc: For the Church, that in this Season of the Apostles she may teach the nations as one taught by God.
For catechists, teachers and parents, that they may pass on the faith with wisdom and love.
For students preparing for examinations and choosing their studies, that they may seek true wisdom.
For parishes and communities divided over leaders and movements, that they may find unity in Christ.
For the dying, that the bread of life may carry them through death to eternal life.
pm.close: Father, you teach all your children and draw them to your Son. Make us humble enough to learn, hungry enough to receive the bread of life, and faithful enough to belong to Christ in everything. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we celebrated the Body and Blood of Christ. Today Jesus tells us how we come to that bread: “It is written in the prophets, ‘And they shall all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to me” (John 6:45).

Before we eat, we listen. That is why every Qurbana begins with the Word: the readings, the Gospel and the homily. God teaches us first, and then feeds us. Let us not arrive late for the readings, as if only the second part mattered.

Then Jesus says: “I am the bread of life.” The ancestors ate manna in the desert and still died. But whoever eats the bread that comes down from heaven will not die. Jesus gives a life that death cannot destroy. And he says first: whoever believes has eternal life. We come to the altar with faith.

Paul tells the proud Corinthians: the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. They were fighting over their favourite preachers, Paul, Apollos and Cephas. Paul says: all of them are yours, and you belong to Christ (1 Corinthians 3:21–23).

So let us become humble learners, like children. Let us not divide our parishes over preachers and movements. All the gifts of the Church are given to us, so that we may belong more fully to Christ, who is the bread of life. Amen.
kids: Children, in the desert God gave his people a special bread called manna. But Jesus says he is an even better bread: the bread of life! At the Holy Qurbana we first listen to God's word, and then we receive Jesus. So listen carefully to the readings next Sunday!

concl: God teaches us at the table of the Word and feeds us at the table of the Body and Blood.
We belong to no party but to Christ, the bread of life, who belongs to the Father.
2027-05-28.resolve: This week, prepare for Sunday by reading the Gospel, make a daily spiritual communion, and make peace where you have taken sides.
